=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:328-329 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]

  WHY: A command such as `perl -I lib -pi -e ...` returns no deny decision and reaches the normal permission flow; severity was rated MAJOR by five reviewers and BLOCKER by minimax_minimax-m3, so the highest severity is used.

  WHY: A separated Perl option argument can stop parsing before the in-place flag and leave the inline edit without a deny decision.
- .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:324-333 | severity=high | confidence=[5]

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Issue #4858 §1 lists “.replace( followed by a write” among the program-text write patterns the hook must recognize.
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py `_PYTHON_WRITE_PATTERNS` tuple and `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `_PYTHON_WRITE_PATTERNS` matches `os.replace` but has no pattern for `Path.replace()`; the tests contain no `Path('x').replace('y')` case.
- requirement: Issue #4858 section 8 calls for `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py` to cover `perl -pi` in-place edit shapes, including separated option arguments before the in-place flag.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py::test_inline_writes_are_denied` parametrize list
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: Existing Perl deny cases cover basic `perl -pi`, `perl -i.bak`, and `perl -0777 -pi` forms but omit `perl -I lib -pi`; the test list also omits the separated Ruby `-F` form.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:329 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Perl flags `I`, `x`, `F`, `D`, and `C` are classified as attached-only even though they accept separate arguments, so `_switch_in_place` may stop before checking a later `-pi` flag.
  WHY: For example, `perl -I lib -pi ...` reaches the non-option argument `lib` and returns False before detecting the in-place edit; the template copy has the same defect.
- .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:333 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Ruby flags `F`, `K`, `W`, and `x` are classified as attached-only even though they accept separate arguments, so `_switch_in_place` may stop before checking a later `-i` flag.
  WHY: For example, `ruby -F , -i -pe ...` reaches the non-option argument before detecting the in-place edit; the template copy has the same defect.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Issue #4858 section 1 lists ".replace( followed by a write" among the program-text write patterns the hook must match, alongside os.replace and Path(...).unlink.
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py _PYTHON_WRITE_PATTERNS tuple at lines 137-147
  Evidence of absence: The tuple matches os.replace, os.rename, os.renames, os.remove, and .unlink( but has no pattern for Path.replace(. No test case exercises Path('x').replace('y').
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:328-330 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Perl `-I` is classified as `attached_value` rather than `next_value`, so the parser does not consume a separate include-directory argument before checking for an in-place flag.
  WHY: For `perl -I lib -pi ...`, `_switch_in_place` encounters `lib`, returns False, and the inline edit reaches the normal permission flow.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:328-330 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The template classifies Perl `-I` as `attached_value` rather than `next_value`, causing the same parser failure for consumer repositories.
  WHY: With a separated include-directory argument, `_switch_in_place` returns False before reaching the in-place flag.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Issue #4858 section 8 requires `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py` to cover `perl -pi` in-place edit shapes.
  Expected change site: tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py in `test_inline_writes_are_denied` parametrize list around lines 153-156
  Evidence of absence: The parametrize list exercises `perl -pi -e`, `perl -i.bak -pe`, and `perl -0777 -pi`, but contains no test case with separated option arguments before the in-place flags, such as `perl -I <dir> -pi -e ...`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:328-329, 312-317 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Perl `-I`, `-M`, and `-m` accept separate arguments but are classified as `attached_value` only, allowing parsing to stop before a later `-pi` flag.
  WHY: For `perl -I lib -pi ...`, `_switch_in_place` encounters `lib` and returns False, so the inline edit reaches the permission prompt.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py:332-333 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Ruby `-x` accepts a separate directory argument but is classified as `attached_value` only, allowing parsing to stop before a later `-pi` flag.
  WHY: `ruby -x lib -pi ...` returns False from `_switch_in_place`, so the inline edit reaches the permission flow.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Issue #4858 §1 "Match" lists the program-text write patterns the hook must recognise, including ".replace( followed by a write" alongside `os.replace` and `Path(...).unlink`.
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/inline_edit_guard.py `_PYTHON_WRITE_PATTERNS` tuple (lines 137-147), and a matching deny case in `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py::test_inline_writes_are_denied` parametrize list.
  Evidence of absence: `re.compile(r"\bos\.(?:replace|rename|renames|remove)\s*\(")` is the only `replace` pattern; there is no `re.compile(r"\.replace\s*\(")` entry. A grep of `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py` shows no `Path('x').replace(` or `Path("x").replace(` entry in the parametrize list.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Issue #4858 §8 calls for `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py` to cover `sed -i` and `perl -pi` in-place edit shapes, and the test "denied" list explicitly says "plus `sed -i`, `perl -pi`".
  Expected change site: `tests/test_inline_edit_guard.py::test_inline_writes_are_denied` parametrize list, around lines 240-243 (the `perl` cluster cases).
  Evidence of absence: Grep of the file for `perl -I` returns no deny case; the copilot review comment id 4151386340 on this PR explicitly calls this out. Without this case, a regression that drops `-I` from `attached_value` to `next_value` (the right fix for the bug above) could not be validated, and the bug it fixes would re-regress silently.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
